subproblems.title: Scalar weight controlled by the multivector difference via a norming covector
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. For an n-covector α on ℝ^P (an element of Covector (Euclid P) n, i.e. a continuous alternating map), let ‖α‖ be its operator norm and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α its Euclidean coefficient norm. MultiVector P n = Λ_n(ℝ^P) is the space of continuous linear functionals on n-covectors, with operator norm ‖·‖ and [0,∞]-valued norm ‖·‖ₑ. Let ζx, ζa ∈ MultiVector P n and t, t₀, C ∈ ℝ with t₀ ≥ 0 and C ≥ 0. Assume ‖α‖ ≤ C·|α| and |ζa(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α, and that there is an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζx(β) = 1. Then, in [0,∞], ofReal t ≤ ofReal t₀ + ofReal C · ‖t•ζx − t₀•ζa‖ₑ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ζx ζa : MultiVector P n) (t t₀ C : ℝ), 0 ≤ t₀ → 0 ≤ C → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ‖α‖ ≤ C * covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ζa α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ζx β = 1) → ENNReal.ofReal t ≤ ENNReal.ofReal t₀ + ENNReal.ofReal C * ‖t • ζx - t₀ • ζa‖ₑ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (fact F2) of the parent proof, with the operator-norm comparison ‖α‖ ≤ C|α| as a hypothesis.
Notation: |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm. For an n-covector α, ‖α‖ is its operator norm as a continuous alternating map. For d ∈ MultiVector P n = (Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ), ‖d‖ is the operator norm and ‖d‖ₑ = ofReal ‖d‖.
1. By hypothesis, choose an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζx(β) = 1. Put d := t•ζx − t₀•ζa ∈ MultiVector P n.
2. Evaluating a continuous linear map at β is linear in the map (ContinuousLinearMap.sub_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul). So d(β) = t·ζx(β) − t₀·ζa(β) = t − t₀·ζa(β).
3. By le_abs_self and the hypothesis on ζa, ζa(β) ≤ |ζa(β)| ≤ |β| ≤ 1. Since t₀ ≥ 0, t₀·ζa(β) ≤ t₀ (mul_le_of_le_one_right).
4. By the comparison hypothesis, ‖β‖ ≤ C·|β|. Since C ≥ 0 and |β| ≤ 1, C·|β| ≤ C (mul_le_of_le_one_right). Hence ‖β‖ ≤ C.
5. We have d(β) ≤ |d(β)| = ‖d(β)‖ ≤ ‖d‖·‖β‖ by ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm applied to d at β. By step 4 and ‖d‖ ≥ 0 (norm_nonneg d, mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left), this is ≤ ‖d‖·C = C·‖d‖.
6. By step 2, t = d(β) + t₀·ζa(β). Steps 5 and 3 then give t ≤ C‖d‖ + t₀, i.e. t ≤ t₀ + C‖d‖ (linarith).
7. ENNReal.ofReal is monotone (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal), so ofReal t ≤ ofReal(t₀ + C‖d‖). Since t₀ ≥ 0 and C‖d‖ ≥ 0 (mul_nonneg with norm_nonneg d), ENNReal.ofReal_add gives ofReal(t₀ + C‖d‖) = ofReal t₀ + ofReal(C‖d‖). Since C ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_mul gives ofReal(C‖d‖) = ofReal C · ofReal‖d‖. Finally ofReal‖d‖ = ‖d‖ₑ by ofReal_norm d (ofReal_norm_eq_enorm is its deprecated alias). Hence ofReal t ≤ ofReal t₀ + ofReal C · ‖t•ζx − t₀•ζa‖ₑ. ∎
Lean remark: the norm on MultiVector P n elaborates as ContinuousLinearMap.hasOpNorm. Generic lemmas unify with it when the element is given explicitly (norm_nonneg d, ofReal_norm d, d.le_opNorm β). With an implicit argument, `rw [ofReal_norm]` does not find its pattern.
proof_key_steps: Pick the norming covector β of ζx (|β| ≤ 1, ζx(β) = 1) and set d := t•ζx − t₀•ζa, so that d(β) = t − t₀·ζa(β).
t₀·ζa(β) ≤ t₀, from ζa(β) ≤ |ζa(β)| ≤ |β| ≤ 1 and t₀ ≥ 0.
d(β) ≤ ‖d‖·‖β‖ ≤ C‖d‖, by le_opNorm and ‖β‖ ≤ C|β| ≤ C.
Hence t ≤ t₀ + C‖d‖; then ofReal_add, ofReal_mul and ofReal_norm give the [0,∞] form.

subproblems.title: Weighted Hausdorff measure of a Borel set under a pointwise weight bound
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P. Let M, B, B' ⊆ ℝ^P with M and B Borel and B ⊆ B'. Let θ : ℝ^P → ℝ and g : ℝ^P → [0,∞], and let c, K ∈ [0,∞] with K ≠ ∞. Let μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(x ↦ ofReal θ(x)), and assume ofReal θ(x) ≤ c + K·g(x) for every x ∈ M. Then μ(B) ≤ c·Hⁿ(M ∩ B) + K·∫⁻_{M∩B'} g dHⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (M B B' : Set (Euclid P)) (θ : Euclid P → ℝ) (g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞) (c K : ℝ≥0∞), MeasurableSet M → MeasurableSet B → B ⊆ B' → K ≠ ∞ → μ = (μHE[n].restrict M).withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (θ x)) → (∀ x ∈ M, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ≤ c + K * g x) → μ B ≤ c * μHE[n] (M ∩ B) + K * ∫⁻ x in M ∩ B', g x ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (mass of balls) of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary Borel set B ⊆ B', an arbitrary integrand g and constants c, K.
1. Substitute the hypothesis μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity(ofReal∘θ). Since B is Borel, withDensity_apply gives μ(B) = ∫⁻ ofReal θ d((Hⁿ⌞M)⌞B). Since B is Borel, Measure.restrict_restrict gives (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞B = Hⁿ⌞(B ∩ M), and B ∩ M = M ∩ B (Set.inter_comm). Hence μ(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} ofReal θ dHⁿ.
2. M ∩ B is Borel (MeasurableSet.inter). Every x ∈ M ∩ B lies in M, so ofReal θ(x) ≤ c + K·g(x) there. Monotonicity of the set integral over a measurable set under a pointwise bound on that set (setLIntegral_mono') gives ∫⁻_{M∩B} ofReal θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩B} (c + K·g) dHⁿ.
3. The constant function x ↦ c is measurable (measurable_const). So lintegral_add_left gives ∫⁻_{M∩B} (c + K·g) dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{M∩B} c dHⁿ + ∫⁻_{M∩B} K·g dHⁿ. By setLIntegral_const, ∫⁻_{M∩B} c dHⁿ = c·Hⁿ(M ∩ B). Since K ≠ ∞, lintegral_const_mul' gives ∫⁻_{M∩B} K·g dHⁿ = K·∫⁻_{M∩B} g dHⁿ; no measurability of g is needed.
4. B ⊆ B' gives M ∩ B ⊆ M ∩ B' (Set.inter_subset_inter_right). Hence ∫⁻_{M∩B} g dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩B'} g dHⁿ (lintegral_mono_set). Multiplying by K and adding c·Hⁿ(M ∩ B) are monotone operations in [0,∞] (gcongr), so c·Hⁿ(M ∩ B) + K·∫⁻_{M∩B} g dHⁿ ≤ c·Hⁿ(M ∩ B) + K·∫⁻_{M∩B'} g dHⁿ.
5. Chaining steps 1–4: μ(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} ofReal θ dHⁿ ≤ c·Hⁿ(M ∩ B) + K·∫⁻_{M∩B} g dHⁿ ≤ c·Hⁿ(M ∩ B) + K·∫⁻_{M∩B'} g dHⁿ. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} ofReal θ dHⁿ, by withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict (B Borel).
Integrate the pointwise bound ofReal θ ≤ c + K·g over the Borel set M ∩ B (setLIntegral_mono').
Split ∫⁻_{M∩B}(c + K·g) = c·Hⁿ(M∩B) + K·∫⁻_{M∩B} g (lintegral_add_left, setLIntegral_const, lintegral_const_mul' with K ≠ ∞).
Enlarge M ∩ B to M ∩ B' in the g-integral (lintegral_mono_set) and use monotonicity.

subproblems.title: Small-radius density bounds from a ball-mass inequality and liminf/limsup/Tendsto hypotheses
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, ω_n = unitBallVolume n (the volume of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ) and V(r) = ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ). Let m, h, H, o : ℝ → [0,∞]. Let θ₀, η₁ ∈ ℝ with θ₀ > 0 and η₁ > 0, and let K ∈ [0,∞] with K ≠ ∞. All limits below are taken as r ↓ 0, i.e. along the filter 𝓝[>] 0. Assume (B) m(r) ≤ ofReal θ₀·h(r) + K·o(r) for all r > 0; (L) ofReal η₁ ≤ liminf m(r)/V(r); (U) limsup H(r)/V(r) ≤ 1; and (D) o(r)/V(r) → 0. Then there is r₀ > 0 such that for all r with 0 < r < r₀: ofReal(η₁/(4θ₀))·V(r) ≤ h(r) and H(r) ≤ 2·V(r).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (m h H o : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (θ₀ η₁ : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0∞), 0 < θ₀ → 0 < η₁ → K ≠ ∞ → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → m r ≤ ENNReal.ofReal θ₀ * h r + K * o r) → ENNReal.ofReal η₁ ≤ liminf (fun r : ℝ => m r / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) → limsup (fun r : ℝ => H r / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ 1 → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => o r / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → ∃ r₀ : ℝ, 0 < r₀ ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < r₀ → ENNReal.ofReal (η₁ / (4 * θ₀)) * (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n)) ≤ h r ∧ H r ≤ 2 * (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3 and 4 of the parent proof, with the ball-mass inequality (B) as a hypothesis.
Notation: ω_n := unitBallVolume n = volume(ball (0 : Euclid n) 1) and V(r) := ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ).
1. (V(r) is positive and finite.) Unfold unitBallVolume: ω_n is the volume of an open ball of positive radius in the finite-dimensional Euclidean space Euclid n. The volume is an open-positive measure, so ω_n > 0 (Metric.measure_ball_pos volume 0 one_pos). It is finite on compacts and Euclid n is proper, so ω_n < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). For r > 0, rⁿ > 0 (pow_pos), so ofReal(rⁿ) > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos); also ofReal(rⁿ) ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top). Hence V(r) ≠ 0 for r > 0 (mul_ne_zero) and V(r) ≠ ∞ for every r (ENNReal.mul_ne_top).
2. (a) Since η₁ > 0, η₁/2 < η₁, so ofReal(η₁/2) < ofReal η₁ (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff). With (L), ofReal(η₁/2) < liminf m(r)/V(r). By Filter.eventually_lt_of_lt_liminf, ofReal(η₁/2) < m(r)/V(r) eventually in 𝓝[>] 0. In the complete lattice [0,∞] the boundedness side condition holds automatically: apply the lemma with all explicit arguments via exact, and its default autoParam discharges it.
3. (b) By (D) and K ≠ ∞, ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul gives K·(o(r)/V(r)) → K·0 = 0 along 𝓝[>] 0 (rewrite with mul_zero). Since η₁/4 > 0, ofReal(η₁/4) > 0, so by tendsto_order, K·(o(r)/V(r)) < ofReal(η₁/4) eventually in 𝓝[>] 0.
4. (c) By (U), limsup H(r)/V(r) ≤ 1 < 2. So by Filter.eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt, H(r)/V(r) < 2 eventually in 𝓝[>] 0 (same remark on the autoParam).
5. The conjunction of (a), (b) and (c) holds eventually in 𝓝[>] 0 (Filter.Eventually.and). By mem_nhdsGT_iff_exists_Ioo_subset there is r₀ > 0 such that (a), (b) and (c) hold for every r ∈ (0, r₀). Fix such an r and write V := V(r); by step 1, V ≠ 0 and V ≠ ∞.
6. (Clearing denominators.) From (a), ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt (with V ≠ 0, V ≠ ∞) gives ofReal(η₁/2)·V < m(r), so ofReal(η₁/2)·V ≤ m(r). From (b), K·(o(r)/V) = (K·o(r))/V (mul_div_assoc), so ENNReal.div_lt_iff gives K·o(r) < ofReal(η₁/4)·V, hence K·o(r) ≤ ofReal(η₁/4)·V. From (c), ENNReal.div_lt_iff gives H(r) < 2·V, hence H(r) ≤ 2·V(r): this is the asserted upper bound.
7. (Splitting.) η₁/2 = η₁/4 + η₁/4 with both summands ≥ 0. So ofReal(η₁/2) = ofReal(η₁/4) + ofReal(η₁/4) (ENNReal.ofReal_add, ring), and ofReal(η₁/2)·V = ofReal(η₁/4)·V + ofReal(η₁/4)·V (add_mul).
8. (Cancelling.) By step 7, step 6, hypothesis (B) at r > 0, and step 6 again: ofReal(η₁/4)·V + ofReal(η₁/4)·V = ofReal(η₁/2)·V ≤ m(r) ≤ ofReal θ₀·h(r) + K·o(r) ≤ ofReal θ₀·h(r) + ofReal(η₁/4)·V (gcongr). The summand ofReal(η₁/4)·V is finite (ENNReal.mul_ne_top with ofReal_ne_top and V ≠ ∞). Cancelling it on the right (ENNReal.add_le_add_iff_right) gives ofReal(η₁/4)·V ≤ ofReal θ₀·h(r).
9. (Dividing by θ₀.) Since θ₀ > 0, ofReal θ₀ ≠ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos) and ofReal θ₀ ≠ ∞. Next, (ofReal θ₀)⁻¹ = ofReal(θ₀⁻¹) (ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos), and ofReal(θ₀⁻¹)·ofReal(η₁/4) = ofReal(θ₀⁻¹·(η₁/4)) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, θ₀⁻¹ ≥ 0). Since θ₀⁻¹·(η₁/4) = η₁/(4θ₀) (field_simp, θ₀ ≠ 0), we get ofReal(η₁/(4θ₀)) = (ofReal θ₀)⁻¹·ofReal(η₁/4). Therefore ofReal(η₁/(4θ₀))·V = (ofReal θ₀)⁻¹·(ofReal(η₁/4)·V) (mul_assoc). By step 8 and monotonicity of multiplication, this is ≤ (ofReal θ₀)⁻¹·(ofReal θ₀·h(r)). That equals h(r) by mul_assoc, ENNReal.inv_mul_cancel (ofReal θ₀ ≠ 0, ≠ ∞) and one_mul. This is the asserted lower bound. Together with step 6, both bounds hold for every r with 0 < r < r₀. ∎
proof_key_steps: V(r) = ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ) ∈ (0,∞) for r > 0, by Metric.measure_ball_pos and measure_ball_lt_top for the unit ball of Euclid n.
Eventually in 𝓝[>] 0: ofReal(η₁/2) < m/V by (L), K·(o/V) < ofReal(η₁/4) by (D), and H/V < 2 by (U). Choose r₀ via mem_nhdsGT_iff_exists_Ioo_subset.
Clear denominators for 0 < r < r₀: ofReal(η₁/2)·V ≤ m(r), K·o(r) ≤ ofReal(η₁/4)·V, and H(r) ≤ 2V.
Split ofReal(η₁/2)·V into two quarters, combine with (B), and cancel the finite quarter: ofReal(η₁/4)·V ≤ ofReal θ₀·h(r).
Divide by ofReal θ₀ ∈ (0,∞): ofReal(η₁/(4θ₀))·V ≤ h(r).
